headline: Parliamentary Archives Committee to Introduce 'Historical Photo Sensitivity Training' for Lawmakers
body:
The Parliamentary Archives Committee announced today that all members of the House must undergo a mandatory three-day workshop on the proper use of historical photography in heated debates. The initiative comes after a frantic week where legislators spent more time scouring the 1970s microfiche archives for vintage political handshakes than discussing the actual floor agenda.

"We noticed a disturbing trend where the speed of a retort is being measured in black-and-white print resolution," said Brijesh Kumar, the Committee’s newly appointed Director of Visual Retorts. "Lawmakers are currently neglecting their committee reports because they are busy arguing over whether a grainy 1974 handshake in Havana constitutes a diplomatic breach or merely a very enthusiastic greeting."

Under the new guidelines, any member attempting to use a photograph of a historical figure to deflect a contemporary jab will be required to submit a notarized 'contextual affidavit.' This document must explain why a forty-year-old photo of a state dinner is legally relevant to a heated argument about current infrastructure projects. If a member cannot explain the connection, they are limited to using modern stock photos of generic high-fives.

"The goal is to move the House from a 'Vintage Instagram Account' model of governance to a more policy-focused approach," added Kumar. "Our archives department is currently overwhelmed by requests for photos of world leaders sitting on furniture that no longer exists. We have had to put a moratorium on requests for anything involving 70s-era neckties to prevent further confusion in the lower house."
caption: MPs ordered to stop treating legislative debates like a Pinterest mood board of the Cold War era. Time to put the scrapbooks away and pick up the policy papers. #Parliament #HistoryBuffs #LegislativeHumor #IndiaPolitics (satire)

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 excels by grounding the absurdity in a specific, bureaucratic initiative—the 'Historical Photo Sensitivity Training'—and providing hilarious invented details like the 'notarized contextual affidavit.' It maintains a perfect deadpan tone throughout, positioning the archive department as a relatable, overwhelmed institution rather than a target of cynicism.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictional committee official and generalized, humorous scenarios about parliamentary conduct to create satire. It does not name specific real-world politicians or institutions in a way that suggests actual misconduct or harm, and the image prompt describes a generic, non-identifiable scene.
